findings: Units that matter most for small district shops: dona (by far the most common: almost every packaged non-food item is priced per piece, with the weight or volume as a size, e.g. 'Kir yuvish kukuni 3 kg - dona'), kg (loose goods: mix, sim, sochma kukun, yem, ko'mir, paxta), qop (sement, gips, yem, o'g'it, ko'mir, always with the weight: 'qop 50 kg'), metr (sim, quvur, shlang, gazlama, zanjir, arqon), qadoq/pachka (salfetka, tagliklar, shurup, A4 500 varaq), rulon (oboy, ruberoid, hojatxona qog'ozi, skotch), litr for loose oils and antifreeze, m2 (gilam, kafel, laminat, linoleum), kub (qum, shag'al, taxta), list (sheet goods), juft (paypoq, shippak, qo'lqop), to'plam (choyshab, piyola, kalitlar), bog' (gul, usma, rayhon, pichan). Price tags in Uzbekistan read '12 000 so'm / dona', '1 kg', '100 g', '1 m', '1 qop', '1 kub', 'kv.m'. Gram pricing in practice: the tag is per kg or per 100 g (spices, nuts, sweets, tea, xina, urug'), the customer asks for 'yarim kilo', '200 gramm' and the seller weighs; only saffron (za'faron) is priced per 1 g. In the fiscal system (MXIK, online cash register) the official units are dona, kilogramm, gramm, litr, metr, kvadrat metr, kub metr, tonna, juft, to'plam, with dona sub-variants (o'ram, baraban/rulon, tutam/bog'); packaged goods with an identifying MXIK are locked to dona, and from 10 August (recent tax rule) some packaged foods (sugar, rice, pasta, tea) must be sold in kg. Minimal unit set recommendation for Zumda (covers every item here): dona, kg (grams in steps), 100 g (as a price basis on top of grams, display only), litr, metr, m2, kub (m3), qop, qadoq (covers pachka and blok), rulon, list, juft, to'plam, bog', lotok (30 dona). That is 15 units; ml, gramm (1 g), tonna, banka, shisha, tyubik, quti, o'nta and mashina can be mapped onto dona/qadoq/kg/kub with the size in the name and are not needed as separate units. Keep sizes (400 g, 1,5 l, 50 kg, 2x2,5) as variant labels, not units.
